topic: Who was responsible for stealing the trophy: Casey or Tony?

turns.speaker: A
turns.utterance: On the day of the St. Patrick's Day celebration at the grade school, Tony dropped off Casey and Randy in front of the school's lobby in his expensive sports car, promising to pick them up when they were finished [E27]. After the school event, Casey waved to the crowd one last time as he backed through the door and rushed into the empty school hallway [E22]. Soon after, the group discovered that a major incident had occurred: the school's famous trophy, which was displayed on the top shelf of a tall glass case in the lobby, was missing. Over the top shelf, a large hole had been broken through the glass, and where the trophy had been, there was now just an empty shelf [E43]. As concern spread about the stolen trophy, Casey asked, "Does anyone have a key to the display case?" Mr. Carswell replied that he had the only key. During this time, Randy remarked on the situation, and Tony, who was Casey's manager, arrived in the hallway to pick them up and asked how things had gone [E54].
turns.content_fidelity_note: All required evidence was covered chronologically and neutrally, with no argument or conclusion.

turns.speaker: B
turns.utterance: On St. Patrick's Day, two men named Tony and Casey arrived at a grade school, where Casey was scheduled to perform for an assembly. Tony had dropped both Casey and another performer off in front of the school's lobby that morning in his expensive sports car and promised to pick them up after the event was finished [E27]. During the assembly, all the children were gathered in the auditorium to see 'The Mighty Casey.' A staff member reported seeing the valuable football trophy still in its display case as the auditorium doors were closed, just as Casey and another performer came onto the stage [E51]. After the performance ended, Casey left the auditorium and hurried into the empty school hallway [E22]. Soon after, it was discovered that the school's famous trophy had been stolen from the display case in the lobby. Authorities and school staff searched every classroom, every desk, the backstage of the auditorium, the teacher’s lounge, and even the principal's office, but they found no trace of the missing trophy [E62].
turns.content_fidelity_note: All required facts are included in correct chronology without argument or conclusion.

turns.utterance: Casey is guilty of stealing the trophy. Casey expressed interest in getting his picture in the paper by being seen with the trophy and Randy, both dressed up for St. Patrick's Day, and the trophy was described as valuable and a collector's item, worth fifty thousand dollars. This combination of wanting publicity and the trophy’s high value could provide a motive for Casey to steal it for personal gain or attention.
